headline: Notebandi's missing money
captionHeadline: The note ban was meant to trap black money. Then 99.3% of the banned cash walked straight back into the banks.
summary: ₹15.41 lakh crore of ₹500 and ₹1,000 notes were cancelled overnight in November 2016. By the RBI's own count, ₹15.31 lakh crore came back. Only about ₹10,720 crore never returned.
forYou: If the black money never stayed in cash, it was already somewhere else. Gold. Property. Abroad.
cta: Send this to the uncle who still says "notebandi finished black money". Follow @postr.news: File #02 drops next.

slides.label: 8 NOV 2016
slides.body: The Prime Minister comes on TV. In *four hours*, every ₹500 and ₹1,000 note becomes paper.
slides.title: 8:00 PM

slides.label: THE PANIC
slides.body: 86% of India's cash. *Gone overnight.* Queues outside every bank and ATM.

slides.label: THE PLAN
slides.title: Trap the hoarders
slides.body: The logic: anyone sitting on sacks of black cash can't walk into a bank and deposit it without being asked where it came from. So that money would simply die.

slides.label: THE COUNT
slides.body: Then the RBI started counting what came back. *It took almost two years.*

slides.label: THE THEORIES
slides.title: Two ways to explain it
points: There was far less black cash than everyone believed
Or it was pushed back in through other people's accounts
The tax department launched "Operation Clean Money" to chase deposits
The sacks of cash everyone imagined were never found

slides.label: THE TWIST
slides.body: Black money was never really sitting in cash. It was in *gold*, in *land*, and *abroad*.
slides.title: THE LIKELY ANSWER

slides.label: BUT
slides.body: Some of it was still in cash. *₹351 crore* of it, in cupboards, seven years later.

headline: ₹351 crore cash
source: Income Tax Department searches, Dec 2023 (as reported by PTI and others)
captionHeadline: ₹351 crore. In cash. Officers needed 36 counting machines and about 10 days to count it.
summary: In December 2023, Income Tax searches on a liquor business group in Odisha found cash stacked in cupboards and bags. It was reported as the biggest cash seizure by any agency in a single operation in India.
forYou: Even the counting machines struggled to keep up.
cta: Send this to someone who thinks they work hard for their money. Follow @postr.news: File #03 drops next.

slides.label: DECEMBER 2023
slides.body: Income Tax officers search premises of a liquor business group in *Odisha*.
slides.title: A TAX SEARCH

slides.label: THEN
slides.body: They open the cupboards. *Bundles.* Then the bags. *More bundles.*

slides.label: THE COUNTING
slides.body: *36* cash-counting machines. Running for about *10 days*.

slides.label: THE RECORD
slides.body: Reported as the *biggest cash seizure* by any agency in a single operation in India.

slides.label: WHY CASH
slides.title: Why anyone keeps this much paper
slides.body: Cash leaves no bank record. No statement, no transfer, no trail. That's exactly why it's the oldest way to hide money, and why a note ban was supposed to kill it.

slides.label: THE QUESTION
slides.body: If this much was in cupboards, *how much was never found?*

slides.label: NEXT FILE
slides.body: Some people don't hide it in cupboards. They hide it *inside a plane toilet.*
